content.title: Paige Bueckers Confirmed Her Relationship With Ex-UConn Teammate in 2025
content.text: If there was ever any doubt that fashion has become central to the WNBA experience, the 2026 draft — the night when teams select new players from a talent pool primarily of college athletes — put it to rest. This year’s rookie class didn’t just arrive in style; they arrived in sync.“This feels like one of the first drafts where every single person feels like they’re going to the same event,” Shanteona Keys, a sports reporter and host of the sports and pop culture podcast Genuinely Curious, tells Yahoo. She attended the draft in New York City on Monday night, where she saw Azzi Fudd’s custom silver Coach gown and Cotie McMahon’s tailored suit dress up close. “It was cohesive enough across the board. It also felt the most curated, which I think is important.”That cohesion marks a notable shift from previous years, when disparities in access to stylists, sponsorships and NIL — name, image and likeness laws that allow collegiate players to profit off of their personal brand — money were often visible on the red (or, in this case, orange) carpet. Paige Bueckers might have had Louis Vuitton money thanks to brand endorsements, but not everyone could splash out on designer labels. This year, that gap appeared to shrink.“Everyone felt like they’re on the same level,” says Keys — without sacrificing personality.Players leaned into a more elevated, intentional sense of self-expression. Outfit changes emerged as a defining trend, with Fudd changing gowns between the carpet and the ceremony, while Olivia Miles switched up both her outfit and hairstyle.“That seems to be something that the really stylish girls are diving into. More looks, more variety,” says Keys. The result? “[Miles’s] aura grows in that sense. And her brand grows.”That level of polish reflects a growing investment in image making throughout the league. Stylists are becoming standard, and brands are getting involved earlier. Coach, in particular, has made a strong push into the WNBA pipeline, partnering with rookies and aligning itself with a new generation of players.“It was smart by them and very strategic,” says Keys of the league’s three-year partnership with the brand. “It brings credibility in both directions. It gives credibility to the WNBA in the fashion world. Then the women of the W give Coach credibility in standing behind this product that is booming and growing every day.”Not long ago, even established stars struggled to secure relationships with major fashion houses. Now, players are entering the league with those doors already open and a clearer understanding of how to build and monetize their personal brands. Once they make the jump to the WNBA, that visibility only expands.In recent years, pregame tunnel fits — the walk from the arena entrance to the locker room — have emerged as the league’s most visible style stage where players consistently showcase their identities before every game. Borrowed from the NBA but redefined, the tunnel now functions as a daily runway, with players like Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese stepping out in Prada and Dior.That evolution is especially significant given the league’s history. For years, WNBA players faced expectations that limited self-expression.“There was a lot of stigma and fear and some directives on how to present yourself,” women’s sports researcher Risa Isard previously told Yahoo. “That was largely in a way that would be quote-unquote ‘nonthreatening’ and traditionally feminine.”The rise of tunnel fits has helped to undo that, giving players a platform to show who they are on their own terms, from streetwear to high fashion. It’s also where the groundwork laid on draft night pays off. The same stylists, partnerships and brand awareness that shape a player’s first appearance as a pro carry over into the regular season — fueling social media growth, deepening fan connection and opening the door to more endorsement opportunities.By the time these 2026 rookies hit the tunnel, they’re not just athletes adjusting to a new league. They’re fully formed brands.“The styling caught up. … There’s a clear vision,” says Keys. “Women’s basketball is high fashion now. It’s just that simple.”Check out some of our favorite looks below.Azzi FuddNo. 1 pick Azzi Fudd couldn't settle on just one look for the big night.(Cindy Ord)Fudd switched into another sequin dress for the ceremony.(Brian Babineau)The UConn alum was selected first overall for the Dallas Wings. She arrived on the orange carpet in a sparkly silver dress with a peekaboo bra detail and high slit, then changed into another sequin number for the ceremony. Both looks were custom Coach.Flau'jae JohnsonLSU guard Flau'jae Johnson was the epitome of glamour on the orange carpet.(Catalina Fragoso)Flau'jae Johnson arrived in a black velvet dress with cutouts by Bent Kahina and a custom fur stole. She’s joining the Seattle Storm.Cotie McMahonCotie McMahon posted content about her outfit ahead of the 2026 WNBA Draft.(Cindy Ord)McMahon’s maroon pinstripe suit dress, paired with a bejeweled bag and strappy black heels over a pair of tube socks, was a fan favorite. The Ole Miss alum was the 11th pick with the Washington Mystics.Marta SuarezMarta Suarez of Spain added a personal touch to her look with a hand-painted purse.(Cindy Ord)Marta Suarez stood out in a bright red suit complete with a waist-cinching black belt and an undone tie. She carried a bag that she had painted herself and showcased signatures from other draftees. The Spanish player is now a Golden State Valkyrie.Raven JohnsonRaven Johnson was dressed by Brittany Hampton, a stylist popular among athletes.(Catalina Fragoso)South Carolina guard Raven Johnson was wearing a patchwork blazer-style dress with black platform heels when she was selected 10th overall by the Indiana Fever.Awa Fam ThiamAwa Fam Thiam, a player from Spain, looked ravishing in red.(Kristina Bumphrey)Awa Fam Thiam was hard to miss in a beautiful red gown with plenty of cutouts. Hailing from Spain, she was the No. 3 pick for the Seattle Storm.Olivia MilesOlivia Miles posed in a bomber jacket on the orange carpet.(Catalina Fragoso)Miles switched up her hair and her outfit for the ceremony.(Brian Babineau)Olivia Miles was selected by the Minnesota Lynx, and wore two different outfits — and hairstyles — for the occasion. The player noted her hair switch-up on Instagram, writing, “For my fellow Black women with natural hair like mine … be you and be free.”Gabriela JaquezGabriela Jaquez dressed as the star that she is after winning the NCAA championships with UCLA.(Cindy Ord)Gabriela Jaquez’s Coach dress featured a high slit and silver stars, with a leather jacket slung over her shoulders. The NCAA champion was drafted by the Chicago Sky.Gianna KneepkensGianna Kneepkens made history as one of six players from the same NCAA team to be drafted in the same time.(Kristina Bumphrey)The UCLA alum was looking like a Greek goddess in a body-skimming dress with a halter neckline and nude heels. She was selected by the Connecticut Sun.Kiki RiceKiki Rice of UCLA wore a two-piece ensemble decorated with diamond tennis necklaces.(Cindy Ord)Kiki Rice was among the players outfitted by Coach. She became the first-ever draft selection for one of the WNBA’s new expansion teams, the Toronto Tempo.Lauren BettsLauren Betts joined five other UCLA alums to be drafted into the WNBA.(Catalina Fragoso)Lauren Betts shined in a custom Coach slip dress with rhinestone detailing. She was wearing jewelry by Gorjana as she was drafted to the Washington Mystics.Nell AnglomaNell Angloma wowed in white.(Kristina Bumphrey)This monochromatic look with a wrap-style blazer was the perfect mix of professional and stylish. France’s Nell Angloma was the 12th player selected and will be joining the Connecticut Sun.Madina OkotMadina Okot put a spin on business attire with a cropped jacket.(Kristina Bumphrey)Madina Okot wore a red pinstripe suit with a cropped jacket and a matching tie. She was selected by the Atlanta Dream.
